# US-004 — Keep the dashboard in sync with .planr/ changes via incremental SSE patches

**Story ID:** US-004  
**Priority:** P1  
**Tasks:** T-004  
**Status:** Shipped (QA PASS)

## Who uses this and why

A user who is running a `/ship` pipeline or actively editing planning artifacts
in `.planr/` and wants the dashboard to reflect those changes in real time —
without reloading the page and without losing their current view, selected node,
active filters, or graph zoom level. This story makes the dashboard useful as a
live monitor during an active planning session or pipeline run.

## What it does

### Server side — watcher (`lib/dashboard/watcher.mjs`)

`createWatcher(planrDir, options)` returns a `{ start, stop, recompute }` handle.
When started, it observes `.planr/` using `fs.watch` with `{ recursive: true }`.
If the platform does not support recursive watching (or if `fs.watch` throws), it
falls back to a polling loop that scans file modification times every 750ms.

A burst of file changes within a 300ms window is coalesced into a single
recompute via a debounce timer. After the debounce fires, `recompute(changedId)`
calls `buildGraph(planrDir, { scope: changedId })` — passing the changed artifact
id as a scope hint so the graph engine can narrow its work — then diffs the
result against the last known snapshot using `diffGraphs(snapshot, next)`.

`diffGraphs` produces a minimal patch:

```
{
  updated: Node[],            // nodes present in both whose content changed
  added: Node[],              // nodes new to next
  removed: string[],          // ids present in prev but gone from next
  edges: { added: Edge[], removed: Edge[] }
}
```

If the patch is empty (`isEmptyPatch` returns true), nothing is broadcast. If it
is non-empty, the server's `onWatcherPatch` callback is called.

### Server side — SSE broadcast (`lib/dashboard/server.mjs`)

The server maintains a `sseClients` Set of open response streams. On every
non-empty patch, it serialises the patch as `data: <json>\n\n` and writes it to
every client. If a write fails (the client disconnected), the client is removed
from the Set. When a client connects to `GET /api/events`, it receives an
immediate `event: ready` message so it knows the stream is live.

The server also applies the patch to its in-memory `currentGraph` cache (via
`applyPatch`) so that a new page load or SSE reconnect sees the up-to-date graph
without a full rebuild.

### Client side — merge (`lib/dashboard/app/main.js`)

`mergePatch(graph, patch)` applies the server's patch to `window.__dashboard.graph`
in place: updated nodes replace by id, added nodes are appended, removed ids are
filtered out, and edges are add/remove-patched. It returns the set of affected
node ids.

After merging, the active view module's optional `partialRefresh(affectedIds)` hook
is called. This gives views the opportunity to repaint only the changed nodes
rather than fully remounting. The router is never re-called, the view hash does
not change, `selectedId` and `filterText` on `window.__dashboard` are not touched.

### `--no-watch` mode

When `--no-watch` is passed to the command, `createDashboardServer({ watch: false })`
is called and the watcher is never started. The `GET /api/events` SSE stream still
emits the initial `ready` event, but no further patches follow. The dashboard
serves a static snapshot of the graph as it was at startup.

## Acceptance criteria (all passing)

- The watcher observes `.planr/` using `fs.watch` (recursive), with polling fallback on platforms where recursive watching is unsupported.
- A burst of saves within the debounce window (≥250ms, ≤500ms — implementation: 300ms) collapses to one recompute. Test: 3 writes within 150ms → 1 patch event (watcher.test.mjs).
- Only the affected subgraph is recomputed (the changed node and its context), not a full rescan.
- The patch pushed over SSE is minimal (`{ updated, added, removed, edges }`).
- The client merges the patch in place without unmounting views, discarding selections, resetting zoom, or clearing filters.
- End-to-end latency ≤1s p95 on a local machine with ≤1 000 nodes (design target; no synthetic benchmark in the test suite, but the debounce + incremental recompute architecture is designed for this target).
- `--no-watch` suppresses the watcher; the SSE stream returns a `ready` event with no subsequent updates.
- On client disconnect, the server removes the response from `sseClients` and the watcher/server stay running for other clients.
- The watcher never writes to `.planr/` under any circumstances (verified by QA grep for `writeFile|writeFileSync|unlink|mkdir` in `watcher.mjs` — zero matches).
